title: NY State Assembly · District 52
area: Downtown Brooklyn, including Brooklyn Heights, DUMBO, Boerum Hill, Cobble Hill, Carroll Gardens and Fort Greene.

context.text: Incumbent Jo Anne Simon (D/WFP), first elected in 2014, defeated Lydia Green 71.1%–28.4% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. She faces Brett Wynkoop (R/C), a perennial candidate who has run against her in 2022 and 2024 and previously ran for New York City Council, in the general election.

candidates.name: Jo Anne Simon

summary.text: Jo Anne Simon is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for NY State Assembly District 52, seeking a seventh term. A disability-rights attorney, she chairs the Assembly's Mental Health Committee and also serves on the Higher Education Committee.

background.text: Grew up in a working-class family in Yonkers, NY, the daughter of Italian immigrants; was the first in her family to attend college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in Communication Sciences from Iona College, a master's degree in Education of the Deaf from Gallaudet University, and a law degree from Fordham University School of Law, completed at night while working full-time.

Worked as a judicial law secretary and taught in Hofstra University School of Law's clinical program before founding a disability civil rights law firm in Downtown Brooklyn; is also an adjunct assistant professor of law at Fordham.
Served as President of the Boerum Hill Association and was a founder or co-founder of several Brooklyn civic organizations, including BrooklynSpeaks.net and the Council of Brooklyn Neighborhoods.
Elected female District Leader and State Committeewoman for the 52nd Assembly District in 2004, before her 2014 election to the Assembly succeeding Joan Millman.

priorities.text: Preserving rent-stabilized housing: "In this increasingly expensive neighborhood, protecting our remaining rent-stabilized housing is more important than ever."
Shifting New York off gas infrastructure toward affordable energy: "We should be accelerating investments in affordable energy that creates jobs and builds a healthier future."

Expanding non-police mental health crisis response: "Tragedies like this underscore the need for greater investment in preventive care and an evidence-based response to mental health crises... We cannot continue to ask police officers to function as mental health care providers."

positions.summary: Joined tenants and a city council member to press a landlord over conditions at rent-stabilized buildings, calling for repairs and protection of tenants' right to stay, and said protecting remaining rent-stabilized housing is increasingly important.
positions.quote: In this increasingly expensive neighborhood, protecting our remaining rent-stabilized housing is more important than ever... I will fight with the tenants of the Riverside Buildings for repairs, accountability, and the right to stay safely in their homes.

positions.summary: Opposed efforts to roll back New York's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, condemned state approval of the NESE gas pipeline, and co-sponsored legislation to move customers off gas infrastructure toward cheaper, cleaner heating alternatives.
positions.quote: Rolling back New York's signature climate law would move the state in the wrong direction. We should be accelerating investments in affordable energy that creates jobs and builds a healthier future.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly's Mental Health Committee and serves as a member of the Higher Education Committee in the 2025–2026 session.

Prime sponsor, with State Senator Liz Krueger, of the Customer Savings and Reliability Act, introduced June 10, 2025, which would end the "100-foot rule" requiring utilities to subsidize new gas-line extensions and amend the gas-service mandate on an opt-out, regional basis.

Prime sponsor of A6004, the Local Input in Community Healthcare Act, requiring advance public notice, a community forum and disclosure before a hospital or critical care unit closes; passed the Assembly and Senate twice, and was vetoed by Governor Hochul in December 2025 after an earlier 2024 veto.

Sponsors a large number of bills each session as a senior Brooklyn Democrat, including A08222 (extending the statute of limitations for certain deed-theft lawsuits and reviving time-barred claims), A10648 (the "utility shutoff protection act") and A03614 (the "New York Stock Act," barring public officers and employees from trading on nonpublic information gained through their official position); as of January 2026 these remained in committee without floor votes.

candidates.researchNotes: Simon has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no 2026 campaign site with dated issue statements could be located; her record here draws on her official Assembly biography, committee assignments and the official bill list, since her sponsored-legislation list (100+ bills) is too large to summarize individually and most remain pending in committee.

candidates.name: Brett Wynkoop
candidates.ballotNote: Previously ran against Jo Anne Simon for this seat in 2022 and 2024, and ran for New York City Council in 2021 and 2025.

summary.text: Brett Wynkoop is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee challenging incumbent Jo Anne Simon for NY State Assembly District 52, a race he has also run in 2022 and 2024. He has also run for New York City Council.
